tips_en: I'd recommend starting with the Superposition Linearity Hypothesis paper (Paper 2) — its novel claim that mixing token embeddings produces a superposition of independent output distributions is both conceptually elegant and practically impactful, yielding ~2× inference throughput. The three papers share a common thread of efficiency-quality trade-offs in modern generative pipelines: FuseReg (Paper 1) improves image generation by decoupling encoder layers for reconstruction vs. diffusion, WanPE (Paper 3) enhances T2V prompts with a 397B model for cinematic planning, and Paper 2 exploits transformer linearity for parallel decoding — all worth reading together if you're interested in how scale, structure, and inference efficiency intersect across vision and language models.
tips_zhao: 建议先阅读第二篇关于“叠加线性假设”的论文——其核心观点是将不同文本流的标记嵌入混合后，输出分布呈现独立分布的叠加，这一新颖假说既具理论美感又有实用价值，可实现约2倍的推理吞吐量。三篇论文共同围绕现代生成流程中效率与质量的权衡：FuseReg（论文1）通过解耦编码器层来提升图像生成中重建与扩散的效果；WanPE（论文3）用3970亿参数的模型增强文生视频提示以实现电影级规划；论文2则利用Transformer的线性特性实现并行解码——若你对视觉与语言模型中规模、结构和推理效率的交叉议题感兴趣，这三篇值得一并研读。
